title: Fujitsu and New Mexico to Establish Quantum Computing Research Center
source_used: Office of the Governor of New Mexico (press release, read on governor.state.nm.us; HPCwire page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham announced a collaboration with Tokyo-based Fujitsu to set up a quantum computing research center in New Mexico.
The center will cover quantum hardware, software, algorithms and theory, and support education and workforce programmes.
It builds on a 2025 agreement between Fujitsu and New Mexico State University on research tied to the FUJITSU-MONAKA processor.
Fujitsu will also work with the Quantum New Mexico Institute at the University of New Mexico on algorithms, applications and systems.
The announcement follows the governor's trade missions to Japan; five quantum companies have come to the state in under two years.
The release gives no investment figure, opening date or job numbers.
quote_evidence: The center will focus on quantum computing hardware, software, algorithms and theory, and will support education and workforce programs to develop New Mexico's quantum talent pipeline.

Under the agreement announced today, Fujitsu and the State of New Mexico aim to expand that work into quantum computing and hybrid computing systems that combine classical computing, artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
why_it_matters_hint: A major foreign tech firm is basing quantum research in a state with national laboratories.
notes: HPCwire copy blocked (403); the original release is from the governor's office. Other outlets covering it: KRQE, Source New Mexico, The Business Journals (headlines only).
